row.vendor: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform (Ansible Tower)
row.team_price_text: Standard: Contact Sales (customized quote by sizing)
row.evidence: Red Hat prices Ansible Automation Platform (Standard and Premium) by customized quote, and the 2.6 authentication docs list local, LDAP, SAML, TACACS+, Entra ID, Google OAuth2, RADIUS, OIDC, Keycloak and GitHub authenticators with no SCIM endpoint.
row.notes: New row. Ansible Tower is sold today as Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform (automation controller behind the platform gateway); researched AAP 2.6. Subscriptions (Standard 9-5 support, Premium 24x7) are quote-only and per managed-node sizing, not per user, so per-user fields are null; both include the full platform, including SAML/OIDC/LDAP sign-in. No SCIM endpoint is documented (none by absence, confidence medium): users come in just in time when they first sign in through an authenticator (accounts matched by email; authenticator maps assign orgs, teams and roles), or are created in the UI or through the platform gateway REST API. A Red Hat knowledgebase article titled 'Does the Ansible Automation Controller provides SCIM 2.0 Integration for Authentication?' exists, but its answer is subscriber-only. No Okta, Entra, Google, OneLogin or JumpCloud catalogue app was found.

plans.name: Standard
plans.notes: 9 AM to 5 PM support; full platform. Priced by managed-node sizing, not per user.

scim.notes: Recorded as not available by absence: the authenticator list has no SCIM option and no SCIM endpoint appears in the docs searched.

user_api.notes: Docs say users, teams and organizations should be managed through the UI or the platform gateway API; the user endpoint paths are in the downloadable OpenAPI schema, which was not read, so no endpoints are listed.

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP, RADIUS and TACACS+ authenticators with authenticator maps (org, team and role assignment at login)
